newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine firms plan to buy 20,000T U.S. wheat.
newsitem.headline: Philippine firms plan to buy 20,000T U.S. wheat.

text.p: Philippine firms plan to buy 20,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, traders said on Tuesday.
"We will open bids shortly for 20,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat," an executive of one of the buyers told Reuters.
The executive refused to give other details of their wheat requirements, saying bidders were "by invitation only".
Last Thursday, Universal Robina Corp bought 21,000 tonnes of U.S. spring and western white wheat at an average of $193 per tonne, traders involved in the deal said.
Earlier reports said URC bought 25,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.
General Milling Corp also bought 27,000 tonnes of spring and western white wheat, and 8,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for shipment either on the last week of this month or October, traders said.
"The price on General Milling's order will be based on the shipment date," said one trader.
Traders also said Philippine firms bought 18,900 tonnes of U.S. western white wheat last Wednesday at $188 to $189 per tonne through trading firm Mitsui and Co Ltd.
